Theme

Latin word

succēdō

succēdō, succēdere, successī, successum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive; with the dative, or in locum and the genitive

take the place of, take over from, succeed; turn out well, succeed, work; to be successful, to work, to go well (of a thing attempted)

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 2.2.5: succēdere sē in eōrum locum … exīstimet; Caes. BG 5.16 (Lewis & Short): ut integrī et recentēs dēfatīgātīs succēderent

  • success

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 670: hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā; Caes. BG 7.26.1: quod rēs nūlla successerat

  • successful

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 670: hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā; Caes. BG 7.26: quod rēs nūlla successerat (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • sūmat igitur ante omnia parentis ergā discipulōs suōs animum, ac succēdere sē in eōrum locum, ā quibus sibi līberī trādantur, exīstimet

    Let him first of all take on a parent’s feelings towards his pupils, and think of himself as taking the place of those who hand their children over to him.Quint. 2.2.5
